sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Tober is the Irish word for a well. The Monaghan encyclopedia sends the reader to the fuller entry on WELL for the sacred springs of the Celtic lands. Holy wells were places of worship where offerings were made and where rites such as inauguration might be performed. The name appears in many place names, signaling a well that once held the reverence of the local people. Tobereevul, for example, is the well of the fairy queen Aeval, gushing from beneath the crag Craganeevul in County Clare.
